summary.title: Exercism
summary.one_liner: Exercism is a free, community-funded platform for practicing 85 programming languages through coding exercises, CLI submission, automated feedback, and mentoring.
takeaways: Exercism offers coding exercises across 85 programming languages, free of charge.
Exercises can be downloaded and submitted from the terminal via a CLI-first tool.
An in-browser editor lets you try languages without installing them locally.
Automated analysis gives feedback and improvement points on submitted solutions.
Human mentors review code to point out gaps in knowledge and idiomatic conventions; you can also become a mentor.
summary.summary: The Exercism homepage describes a platform for learning programming through practice exercises in 85 languages, with example exercises such as "Allergies", "Zebra Puzzle", and a queens-on-a-chessboard problem. It highlights a CLI-first workflow for downloading and submitting exercises, an in-browser editor, and automatic analysis of solutions. It also promotes free mentoring, where mentors review code to teach idioms and conventions, and mentees are encouraged to mentor others. A note points beginners to a separate platform called Jiki. The page is mostly promotional, so details like pricing beyond "free" are not specified.
